sky._note: Northern-hemisphere evening sky (works for India, Europe, USA). Month = 1..12.

byMonth.1: Find Orion's three-star belt in the evening. Below it hangs the Orion Nebula, a star nursery.
byMonth.2: Orion is high after dark. The red star at its shoulder, Betelgeuse, is a red supergiant.
byMonth.3: Look north for the Saptarishi (Big Dipper) rising in the evening.
byMonth.4: The Saptarishi (Big Dipper) is in the north after dark. Its two end stars point toward Polaris, the Pole Star.
byMonth.5: Bright Arcturus shines in the east. Follow the arc of the Big Dipper's handle to find it.
byMonth.6: Scorpius rises in the south-east with red Antares at its heart.
byMonth.7: On a dark night the Milky Way runs through Scorpius and Sagittarius in the south.
byMonth.8: Find the Summer Triangle overhead: Vega, Deneb and Altair.
byMonth.9: The Summer Triangle is still high in the evening, in the west after dark.
byMonth.10: The Pleiades (Krittika), a tiny cluster of stars, rise in the east later in the evening.
byMonth.11: The Pleiades are up in the east after dark. How many stars can you count?
byMonth.12: Orion climbs over the eastern horizon in the evening.

byPhase.new: No Moon tonight, so it's the best time to look for faint stars.
byPhase.waxingCrescent: A thin Moon after sunset in the west. Look for the dim 'earthshine' on its dark part.
byPhase.firstQuarter: Half Moon! With binoculars, the craters along the shadow line look amazing.
byPhase.waxingGibbous: A bright, nearly full Moon. Its dark patches are old lava plains.
byPhase.full: Full Moon rises at sunset. The Sun, Earth and Moon are lined up.
byPhase.waningGibbous: The Moon rises late in the evening tonight.
byPhase.lastQuarter: Half Moon in the morning sky. Look before school!
byPhase.waningCrescent: A thin Moon before sunrise in the east.
